title: Self-attention, from first principles
subtitle: How a token reads from the tokens before it, and why that makes the next word easier to predict.
audience: For students who know embeddings, dot products, softmax and next-token prediction, and who have not yet met attention.
legendTitle: How to read this page: seven colours, seven objects
provenance: Where the numbers come from: a tiny demonstration model with {{d_model}}-number representations and a {{vocab}}-word vocabulary. Each coordinate was given an illustrative name{{axes}}, and the weights were written by hand so that the names are true. The arithmetic is real, but the model is not a trained language model.

footer: Notation: e is always the current token representation, and Δe is this page's pedagogical name for the attention output. The addition e + Δe is the standard residual connection.
durationLabel: The full walkthrough takes multiple sessions. A classroom route is suggested in Section 1.
hook: The fisherman sat beside the river bank and watched the ___. You know the next word. What would a model have to read to know it too?
